title: What does the XRPL DisallowIncomingTrustline account flag mean?
abstract: Sourced explanation of DisallowIncomingTrustline and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, DisallowIncomingTrustline blocks incoming trust-line creation under the supported amendment rules. [1]

The AccountSet reference includes implicitly created lines from OfferCreate and identifies a cleanup amendment dependency. This setting is different from RequireAuth: one limits creation, while the other controls permission to hold issued balances. Review existing lines and network fixes before designing an issuer onboarding flow around the option. A new configuration does not erase historical relationships. [1][2]

XRPL distinguishes an AccountSet option from the AccountRoot bit that records the resulting state. SetFlag and ClearFlag use option identifiers, while the ledger Flags field stores bit values; the numbers are not interchangeable. Read the documented mapping for DisallowIncomingTrustline and check the validated account state after any permitted change. A successful submission response alone does not establish that the requested state is final. [1][2]

Author interpretation: document why DisallowIncomingTrustline is needed, who may authorize a change and what existing users would experience. Review irreversible settings before issuance and test reversible settings with representative counterparties. This is guidance for interpreting account controls, not a live network measurement. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
